To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the usp45 gene encodes a protein with a tripartite leader peptide, that can be used as signal peptide to secrete a heterologous protein in L. lactissubsp. lactis and that the leader peptide can be used to secrate a homologous protease.

the Usp45 secretion signal is functional in the secretion of the homologue PrtP and the heterologue α-amylase in L. lacti s, and that the Usp signal peptide can be used to direct the secretion of heterologous proteins by L. lactis.
a leader sequence of 27 amino acid residues is sufficient for efficient secretion of α-am ylase in Lactococcus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional characterization of a signal peptide from L. lactis and its application in the secretion of homologous and heterologous proteins in L. lact is.
the functional analysis of a signal peptide from a secreted protein from L. lactis in the secretion of two other proteins.
the development of an efficient signal peptide that can be used for the heterologous secretion of proteins in gram-positive organisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the gram-positive bacterium L. lactis at least the first 27 residues of Usp45 are necessary to secrete a heterologous protein.
a signal peptide of 19 residues is sufficient for the efficient secretion of proteins in E. coli, while in L. lacti s at least 27 residues are required.
the 27 residue usp45 leader peptide is able to secrete both homologous and heterologous proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the usp45 leader peptide is a functional signal peptide for the secretion of homologous proteins and heterologous α- amylase in L. lacti s.
the usp45 signal peptide can be used as a secretion signal for the secretion of a variety of proteins in L. lacti

the 27 residue signal peptide of Usp45 is a versatile leader peptide for the secretion of heterologous proteins in L. lacti s.
